name: Bauchi
summary_text: Bauchi is the only Nigerian state with a carried-out Sharia death-by-stoning sentence for same-sex acts in the modern record: on 28 June 2022 a Sharia Court in Ningi LGA sentenced three men to death under Section 134 of the Bauchi State Sharia Penal Law (2001), following arrest by the Hisbah religious police on 14 June 2022 and conviction on their own admissions; the Hisbah head publicly announced the case. Lower-level practice includes secret floggings (March 2014, four men 15 lashes each, trial held in secret) and a Sharia Commission charging a dozen men with belonging to a 'gay club' (January 2014). LGBTQ+ groups warned the stoning could trigger similar cases across the Sharia block. Mitigating institutional fact: the Upper Sharia Court of Bauchi State has repeatedly quashed stoning sentences on appeal (Babaji 2003, Chiyawa 2003), per Amnesty International. However, the 2022 conviction and announcement demonstrate active enforcement capacity. Score 0.064 below the national 0.08, reflecting the only actual capital-punishment-for-homosexuality event in Nigeria plus ongoing Hisbah arrests. Well below Kano, which has equivalent statutory death-penalty text but no documented carried-out stoning, and far below the generic Sharia states, where enforcement documentation is thinner.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (Reuters returns 401 to automated fetches); the underlying Reuters report (2 July 2022) covers the Ningi Sharia court sentencing three men - a 70-year-old among them - to death by stoning for homosexuality after a 14 June 2022 Hisbah arrest, the first time the death penalty has actually been imposed for homosexuality in Nigeria.

Amnesty International press release (2004): the Upper Sharia Court of Bauchi State quashed Jubrin Babaji's death-by-stoning 'sodomy' sentence (convicted 25 September 2003 under Section 133 of the Bauchi Sharia Penal Code Law 2001) for denial of counsel and a defective confession, following the quashing of Yunusa Rafin Chiyawa's conviction on 14 November 2003 - 'a number of cases where convictions and sentences to death have been quashed on appeal'. Also records a then-pending stoning appeal (Usman/Ibrahim) before a Sharia Court of Appeal in Niger State.
